'''William Allen Casselman''' (born November 27, 1941) is an [[American Canadian]] mathematician who works in [[representation theory]] and [[automorphic forms]]. He is a professor emeritus at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref name="UBC-directory">{{cite web |url=https://www.math.ubc.ca/People/people.shtml?group=Emeriti+and+Retirees |title=Emeriti and Retirees |publisher=[[University of British Columbia]] Mathematics Department |access-date=September 27, 2020 |archive-date=May 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511101950/https://www.math.ubc.ca/People/people.shtml?group=Emeriti+and+Retirees |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is closely connected to the [[Langlands program]] and has been involved in posting all of the work of [[Robert Langlands]] on the internet.<ref>[http://publications.ias.edu/rpl/ Institute for Advanced Study: The Work of Robert Langlands]</ref>

==Career==
Casselman did his undergraduate work at [[Harvard College]] where his advisor was [[Raoul Bott]] and received his PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1966 where his advisor was [[Goro Shimura]]. He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1974, 1983, and 2001.<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/cass Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars: Casselman, William]</ref> He emigrated to Canada in 1971 and is a professor emeritus in mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref name="UBC-directory"/>

==Research==
Casselman specializes in [[representation theory]], [[automorphic forms]], [[geometric combinatorics]], and the structure of [[algebraic groups]]. He has an interest in mathematical graphics<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200701/rev-roegel.pdf ''Mathematical Illustrations: A Manual of Geometry and PostScript'' reviewed by Denis Roegel] in [[Notices of the AMS]]</ref> and has been the graphics editor of the ''Notices of the American Mathematical Society'' since January, 2001.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/editors.html Notices of the American Mathematical Society: Editors and Staff]</ref>

==Awards==
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=2015-11-18}}.</ref>
